title: Check your understanding: Keeping a Contribution Branch Updated

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of keeping a contribution branch updated?
options: Updating a contribution branch starts by fetching the upstream references and reviewing divergence. Choose merge or rebase according to team policy, then resolve conflicts and rerun checks before updating the proposal.
Git automatically backs up every file, including ignored and untracked files, to a remote.
The operation grants every contributor write access to the hosted repository.
questions.answer_key: Updating a contribution branch starts by fetching the upstream references and reviewing divergence. Choose merge or rebase according to team policy, then resolve conflicts and rerun checks before updating the proposal.
questions.explanation: Updating a contribution branch starts by fetching the upstream references and reviewing divergence. Choose merge or rebase according to team policy, then resolve conflicts and rerun checks before updating the proposal.

questions.prompt: Which command is the most direct starting point for this lesson’s example?
questions.explanation: Use `git fetch upstream` as the first inspection/action in the example, and then verify the result with the companion checks in the lesson.

questions.prompt: Which is the safest general practice when working with keeping a contribution branch updated?
options: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
Run the most destructive option first; the reflog guarantees every file can always be recovered.
Assume the local command also changed the remote and satisfied all hosting-platform policies.
questions.answer_key: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
questions.explanation: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
